Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 32, verses 10–11:

Explanation of the words:

"A-idha dalalna fi al-ardi" (Are we, when we have gone astray in the earth?): that is, we have been hidden in it, having perished and become dust.

"A-inna lafi khalqin jadid" (Are we truly in a new creation?): that is, will we return to a new creation after our perishing and our mingling with the dust?

"Bal hum bi-liqa'i rabbihim kafirun" (Nay, they are disbelievers in the meeting with their Lord): that is, the matter did not stop at their denying resurrection; it went beyond to their disbelief in the meeting with their Lord, and it is this that made them deny resurrection.

"Qul yatawaffakum malaku al-mawt" (Say: the Angel of Death will take you in death): that is, the Angel of Death, who is charged with taking souls, will seize your souls.

"Thumma ila rabbikum turja'un" (Then to your Lord you will be returned): that is, after death. And since you do not prevent death from yourselves, you will not prevent life from yourselves either, so your return is certain, without doubt.

The meaning of the two verses:

The discussion continues on establishing the foundations of belief. Allah, exalted is He, informs about those who deny resurrection, saying: "And they say" (﴿وقالُوۤاْ﴾), that is, those who deny the Last Resurrection: "Are we, when we have gone astray in the earth" (﴿أءِذا ضَلَلْنا فِي ٱلأَرْضِ﴾), that is, when we have been hidden in it such that we have become dust in it, "Are we truly in a new creation?" (﴿أءِنّا لَفِي خَلْقٍ جَدِيدٍ﴾), that is, will we indeed return in a new creation? This is from them a denial of resurrection and a deeming it unlikely. Then Allah, exalted, informs of the cause of their denial of resurrection, which is that they are disbelievers in the meeting with their Lord, for if they believed in the meeting with Allah that He had promised them, they would not have denied resurrection and life for that reason. His saying, exalted is He, "Say (﴿قُلْ يَتَوَفّاكُم﴾)," that is, say, O Our Messenger, to these deniers of resurrection and the meeting with the Lord, exalted is He: "He will take you in death (﴿يَتَوَفّاكُم﴾) at the end of your terms" (﴿مَّلَكُ ٱلْمَوْتِ﴾), the angel whom his Lord has entrusted to seize your souls, "Then to your Lord you will be returned" (﴿ثُمَّ إلىٰ رَبِّكُمْ تُرْجَعُونَ﴾) after that. And since you do not repel death from yourselves, how will you repel life when Allah wills it from you? Or have you repelled it when you were nothing, and Allah brought you into existence and gave you life?

Guidance from the two verses:

From the guidance of the two verses:

1) Establishing the belief in resurrection and recompense.

2) The sin which is the cause of every sin is disbelief in the meeting with Allah, exalted is He.

3) Clarification that there is an angel for taking souls, who has assistants from among the angels, and that the earth was made for the Angel of Death like a basin before him, from which he takes whatever he wills.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 32, verses 12–14:

Explanation of the words:

"إذ المجرمون" (Idh al-mujrimun, "when the criminals"): that is, the polytheists who denied the meeting with their Lord.

"ناكسوا رؤوسهم" (nakisu ru'usihim, "bowing their heads"): that is, lowering them in shame, humiliation and disgrace.

"ربنا أبصرنا" (Rabbana abṣarna, "Our Lord, we have seen"): that is, what we used to deny of the Resurrection.

"وسمعنا" (wa sami'na, "and we have heard"): that is, the confirmation of what Your messengers used to command us in the world.

"فارجعنا" (fa-irji'na, "so return us"): that is, to the abode of the world.

"لآتينا كل نفس هداها" (la-atayna kulla nafsin hudaha, "We would have given every soul its guidance"): that is, if We had willed to guide people by compulsion, without their choice, We would have done it.

"ولكن حق القول مني" (wa lakin haqqa al-qawlu minni, "but the word from Me has come due"): that is, it became binding, and it is: "I will surely fill Hell with the jinn and mankind all together."

"إنا نسيناكم" (inna nasinakum, "We have forgotten you"): that is, We have left you in the punishment.

"عذاب الخلد" (adhab al-khuld, "the punishment of eternity"): that is, the everlasting, perpetual punishment.

"بما كنتم تعملون" (bima kuntum ta'malun, "for what you used to do"): of the evil deeds of disbelief, denial, wickedness and shirk.

Explanation of the verses:

The noble context continues to establish the belief in the Resurrection and the recompense, by mentioning its events and what happens to those who deny it in the Hereafter. Allah says: ﴿And if you could see﴾ O Our Messenger, ﴿when the criminals﴾, those who committed crimes against themselves, defiling them with shirk and sins, driven by denial of the meeting with Allah, ﴿have bowed their heads﴾, that is, lowering them before their Lord out of the shame and disgrace that befell them at the Resurrection. You would see a dreadful matter with no equal. As for His saying, ﴿Our Lord, we have seen and heard﴾, this is the speech of the criminals while standing before their Lord, that is: O our Lord, we have now seen what we used to deny of the Resurrection and recompense, and we have heard from You, that is, the confirmation of what Your messengers used to command us in the world. ﴿So return us﴾, that is, to the abode of the world, ﴿that we may do righteousness﴾, that is, righteous deeds, ﴿for we are now certain﴾, that is, now, and no doubt remains in our souls that You are the true God, and that Your meeting is true. As for His saying: ﴿And had We willed, We would have given every soul its guidance﴾, this is because when the criminals demanded to be returned to the world to do righteousness, Allah informed that there is no need to send them back to the world in order to believe and do righteous deeds, for if He had willed to guide them, He would have guided them by compulsion, without their choice. But it had already been decreed that they would enter Hell, so they must enter it, and this is the meaning of His saying: ﴿But the word from Me has come due﴾, that is, the punishment became binding upon them, and this is the meaning of His saying: ﴿I will surely fill Hell with jinn and mankind all together﴾, that is, from the disbelieving and criminal jinn and humans together.

His saying: ﴿So taste﴾, that is, the punishment and disgrace, ﴿because you forgot the meeting of this your Day﴾, that is, because of your forgetting it, ﴿and so you did not believe and did not do righteous deeds. Indeed, We have forgotten you﴾, that is, We have left you in the punishment. ﴿And taste the punishment of eternity for what you used to do﴾, of shirk and sins. This is said to them while they are in Hell, as a rebuke and reproach, an increase in their punishment, and we seek refuge in Allah from the punishment of the Fire.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of these verses:

1) Condemnation of crime and criminals and explanation of their condition on the Day of Resurrection.

2) Explanation that faith does not benefit at the sight of the punishment.

3) Explanation of Allah's decree regarding the filling of Hell with both criminal humans and jinn.

4) Establishment of the principle of causation: deeds are the cause of recompense, whether good or evil.

Explanation of the words:

"Afaman kana mu'minan" (Is one who was a believer): i.e., one who affirms Allah, His Messenger, and the meeting with his Lord.

"Kaman kana fasiqan" (like one who was a defiant transgressor): i.e., a disbeliever. "La yastawun" (They are not equal).

"Jannatu al-ma'wa nuzulan" (Gardens of refuge as a lodging): al-nuzl is what is prepared for a guest as hospitality.

"Min al-'adhab al-adna" (From the lesser punishment): i.e., the punishment of this world, such as affliction with famine, drought, killing, and captivity.

"Al-'adhab al-akbar" (The greater punishment): this is the punishment of the Hereafter in the fire of Jahannam.

"La'allahum yarji'un" (So that perhaps they will return): i.e., He afflicts them with calamities in this world, hoping that they will believe and affirm the Oneness of Allah.

"Wa man adhlamu mimman dhukkira bi-ayati Rabbihi fa-a'rada 'anha" (And who is more unjust than one who is reminded of the signs of his Lord and then turns away from them): no one is ever more unjust than him.

"Inna min al-mujrimina muntaqimun" (Indeed, We will take retribution upon the criminals): i.e., upon the polytheists, by punishing them with the most severe kinds of punishment.

Meaning of the verses:

His statement, the Exalted, "Afaman kana mu'minan kaman kana fasiqan" (Is one who was a believer like one who was a defiant transgressor?), i.e., a disbeliever: the Exalted negates that the disbeliever is equal to the believer. Therefore, after the denying interrogative, He answered with His saying, the Exalted, "La yastawun" (They are not equal). Then the Exalted explained the recompense of the two groups, and thereby the distance between them was confirmed, so He said, "Amma alladhina amanu" (As for those who believed) in Allah as Lord and God, and in Muhammad as Prophet and Messenger, and in Islam as law and religion, "wa 'amilu al-salihat" (and did righteous deeds) by performing the obligatory and voluntary acts of worship generally, after avoiding polytheism and the forbidden things, "fa-lahum jannatu al-ma'wa nuzulan" (then for them are gardens of refuge as a lodging), i.e., hospitality for them, "bima kanu ya'malun" (as a reward for what they used to do). As for those who defied the command of Allah, not affirming His Oneness and not obeying Him, living in polytheism and sins until they died, "fa-ma'wahumu al-nar" (their refuge is the Fire), i.e., their abode, the place of their dwelling and residence, where they will not leave. "Kullama aradu an yakhrujuu minha" (Whenever they wish to get out of it), i.e., whenever they intend to leave it, "u'idu fiha" (they are returned into it) by the guardians of Hell, who push them back from its gates. [As-Sajdah: 10].

His statement, the Exalted, "Wa lanudhiqannahum min al-'adhab al-adna" (And We will surely make them taste the lesser punishment), which is the punishment of this world by famine, high prices, killing, and captivity, "duna al-'adhab al-akbar" (short of the greater punishment), which is the punishment of the Day of Resurrection, "la'allahum yarji'un" (so that perhaps they will return). He, the Exalted, informs that He will do this to the disbelievers of Quraysh, so that perhaps they will repent, return to faith and monotheism, be saved from punishment, and enjoy bliss in Paradise. Indeed, many of them did repent. His statement, "Wa man adhlamu mimman dhukkira bi-ayati Rabbihi thumma a'rada 'anha" (And who is more unjust than one who is reminded of the signs of his Lord and then turns away from them), i.e., he was admonished by them and warned, as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to recite the Qur'an to them, and some of them would turn away from it, not listening to it, and go back while arrogant, we seek refuge with Allah. Such people, there is no one more unjust than them. His statement, the Exalted, "Inna min al-mujrimina muntaqimun" (Indeed, We will take retribution upon the criminals), He, the Exalted, informs that He will certainly take retribution upon the people of crime, who are the people of polytheism and sins. And there was narrated from the Prophet ﷺ the mention of three categories of the specific people of crime, who are:

1) One who "'aqada" (ties) a banner for an unjust cause, i.e., carries a battle standard against the Muslims, being a wrongdoer and not in the right.

2) One who disobeys (ʿaqqa) his parents, i.e., harms them by beating or the like, prevents them their due kindness, and does not obey them in what is right.

3) One who walks with an oppressor to support him. Narrated by Ibn Jarir from Mu'adh ibn Jabal, may Allah be pleased with him.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of these verses:

1) Clarification of the error of one who equates the believer with the disbeliever, the righteous with the wicked, and the obedient with the defiant.

2) Clarification of the recompense of each of the believers and the defiant.

3) Clarification that Allah, the Exalted, was afflicting Quraysh with various kinds of calamities so that perhaps they would repent.

4) Clarification that there is no one more unjust than one who is reminded of the signs of Allah and then turns away from them, arrogantly, denying and obstinately.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 32, verses 23–26:

Explanation of the words:

﴿And We certainly gave Moses the Book﴾: That is, We sent down the Torah to him.

﴿So do not be in doubt about meeting him﴾: That is, do not doubt your meeting with Moses, peace be upon him, on the night of the Isra' (Night Journey) and the Mi'raj (Ascension).

﴿And We made it a guidance for the Children of Israel﴾: That is, We made the Book, the Torah, a guidance, meaning a guide for the Children of Israel.

﴿And We made among them leaders guiding by Our command﴾: That is, We made among the Children of Israel leaders, meaning rightly guided commanders who guide people by Our command to do so and Our permission for it.

﴿And they were certain of Our signs﴾: That is, those guides were certain of the signs of their Lord, His proofs upon His servants, and what the signs carry of promise and warning.

﴿Indeed, your Lord will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection﴾: That is, between the prophets and their nations, and between the believers and the disbelievers, the polytheists and the monotheists.

﴿concerning that about which they used to differ﴾: That is, concerning matters of religion.

﴿Has it not become clear to them﴾: That is, they were heedless and it was not made manifest.

﴿how many generations We destroyed before them﴾: That is, Our destruction of many people of generations before them for their disbelief, their polytheism, and their denial of their messengers.

﴿as they walk through their dwellings﴾: That is, they pass by their homes walking, and these are on their route to al-Sham, such as the cities of Salih, the Dead Sea of Lut, and similar places.

﴿Indeed, in that are signs﴾: That is, indications and signs of the power of Allah the Exalted and the painfulness of His punishment.

﴿Will they not then hear?﴾: That is, they are deaf and do not hear these admonitions and proofs.

Meaning of the verses:

His saying, the Exalted, ﴿And We certainly gave Moses the Book﴾: That is, We gave Moses, son of Imran, one of the prophets of the Children of Israel, the great Book, which is the Torah. Thus, the polytheists should not deny that your Lord gives you the Qur'an, just as He gave Moses the Torah. In this there is an affirmation of a principle of the creed, namely revelation and Muhammadan prophethood. His saying, ﴿So do not be in doubt about meeting him﴾: That is, do not be in doubt, O Muhammad, about your meeting with Moses on the night of the Isra' and Mi'raj, for you met him, and he asked you to return to your Lord regarding the matter of the prayer, so you kept returning until it became five, after it had been fifty. His saying, ﴿And We made it a guidance for the Children of Israel﴾: That is, the Book or Moses, both of them were a guide for the Children of Israel to the path of peace and the straight way.

His saying, ﴿And We made among them leaders﴾: That is, rightly guided commanders who guide people to their Lord, so they believe in Him and worship Him alone, and thereby they are perfected and attain felicity, and that is by His command, the Exalted, to them. His saying, ﴿when they were patient﴾: That is, patient against the harm of their peoples. ﴿And they were certain of Our signs﴾ which carry Our command and Our prohibition, and Our promise and Our warning, ﴿certain﴾: That is, they became qualified to bear the message of the call by two things: patience over harm, and complete certainty in the truth of what they call to and its benefit and efficacy. His saying, the Exalted, ﴿Indeed, your Lord will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that about which they used to differ﴾: He, the Exalted, informs His Messenger Muhammad ﷺ that He, glorified and exalted, is the One who judges between those who differ among the prophets and their nations, and between the monotheists and the polytheists, and the Sunnis and the innovators, so He decides for the felicity of the people of truth and the misery of the people of falsehood. In the verse there is consolation for the Messenger and lightening upon him of what he finds in himself from his people's opposition to him.

His saying, ﴿Has it not become clear to them how many generations We destroyed before them﴾: That is, they were blind, and it was not made clear to them Our destruction of many nations ﴿as they walk through their dwellings﴾, passing by them on their journeys to al-Sham, such as the cities of Salih, the lands of Madyan, and the Dead Sea of Lut, that We are capable of destroying them if they persist in polytheism and denial, just as We destroyed the generations before them. His saying, ﴿Indeed, in that are signs﴾: That is, in Our destruction of the people of the earlier generations when they committed polytheism and denied, there are indications, proofs and demonstrations of the power of Allah and the severity of His vengeance upon those who disbelieve in Him and deny His messenger. His saying, ﴿Will they not then hear?﴾: That is, they are deaf and do not hear these admonitions that are recited to them, so that they might repent from polytheism and denial, and thus be saved and attain felicity.

Guidance from the verses:

1) Affirmation of Muhammadan prophethood and confirmation of the story of the Isra' and Mi'raj.

2) The Book and the Sunnah are both a guide for the servants if they seek guidance in them.

3) Explanation of what attains leadership in religion: patience and soundness of certainty.

4) Every dispute that existed in this life will be concluded by the judgment of Allah the Exalted concerning it on the Day of Resurrection.

5) In Allah the Exalted's destruction of the previous generations is the greatest admonisher for whoever has a heart, hearing, and insight.
